standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherian local ring of dimension two with a nonzerodivisor t, its height one primes above t
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard commutative algebra; the statement writes V(t) = {m, q_1, ..., q_r} for the primes containing t, so the q_i are the height one primes of the two-dimensional local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the geometry of the situation, in particular that only finitely many primes lie above t and that the localizations A_{q_i} are one-dimensional; no part of the gluing construction is taken from it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localization is exact and A is Noetherian
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard commutative algebra; used at proof lines 1122-1124 to conclude that M and M' are finite A-modules with M_{q_i} = M'_{q_i} = B_i
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies exactness of localization and finite generation; the construction of M, M' and B stays inside the counted proof.

core_obligations: Build finite A-modules inside a bounded denominator range: choose n > 0 with B_i contained in t^{-n}A_{q_i}, let M contained in t^{-n}A and M' contained in t^{-2n}A be the A-submodules of elements mapping into B_i, respectively into B_i, inside t^{-n}A_{q_i} respectively t^{-2n}A_{q_i}; Noetherianity makes M and M' finite and exactness of localization gives M_{q_i} = M'_{q_i} = B_i, while M contained in M' (proof lines 1118-1124).
Control the index: since M contained in M' are finite A-modules with the same localizations at every q_i, the quotient M'/M is annihilated by m^c for some c > 0 (proof lines 1124-1125).

Make the glued ring: observe that the multiplication t^{-n}A x t^{-n}A -> t^{-2n}A maps M x M into M', then set B = A + m^{c+1}M, which is a finite A-algebra with B_{q_i} = B_i and B/A annihilated by a power of t; the proof ends by omitting the verification that B is local with maximal ideal m + m^{c+1}M (proof lines 1125-1129).
proof_roadmap: Bound the denominators of the given extensions so that each B_i sits inside t^{-n}A_{q_i}, and define M and M' by the condition that an element maps into B_i in the two localizations (proof lines 1118-1122).
Use Noetherianity and exactness of localization to see that M contained in M' are finite A-modules with M_{q_i} = M'_{q_i} = B_i, hence M'/M is annihilated by some power m^c (proof lines 1122-1125).

Multiply: the product of two elements of M lands in M' because t^{-n}A times t^{-n}A sits in t^{-2n}A, so B = A + m^{c+1}M is a ring, finite over A, with the prescribed localizations, and B/A is killed by a power of t (proof lines 1125-1129).
difficulty_reason: The lemma glues finitely many finite local extensions A_{q_i} contained in B_i, each with B_i/A_{q_i} killed by a power of t, into a single finite extension A contained in B of local rings with B_{q_i} isomorphic to B_i and B/A killed by a power of t (statement lines 1106-1114). The construction is not a direct limit: denominators have to be bounded once and for all by choosing n with B_i contained in t^{-n}A_{q_i}, and the two-step choice of M contained in t^{-2n}A and then of the subring B = A + m^{c+1}M is what forces both the prescribed localizations and the finite generation over the two-dimensional local ring (proof lines 1118-1128). The closing verification that B is local with maximal ideal m + m^{c+1}M is explicitly left unstated by the author, and is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: the argument is short but the two nested bounded-denominator modules are a genuine construction rather than a citation.
